messages:
sophie: Incident bot just flagged high error rates on serving-cluster-prod-us-east-1. Containers are restarting on 3 nodes, customers seeing 502s. 
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2026-0453 - Multiple container restarts due to CUDA illegal memory access. Severity: P2. Pager routed to oncall. 
lee: I can see node flaps in the autoscaler logs, looks like three different G4 nodes reporting OOM + illegal memory access in kernel logs. Metrics: GPU mem jumps then kernel panic. 
raj: Copying kernel log snippet from node gpu-cc-07: ```[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! Status: 0x0000000e 
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, PID=2145, GPU generating an illegal memory access attempt.``` 
sophie: Thanks. Any recent deploys to that model or runtime change? 
deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-15T18:21:03Z - canary trigger - runtime-image v3.8.2 -> v3.9.0 was rolled out to 10% of capacity at 18:21:03Z. Canary still in progress. 
maria: Affected customers: 2 high-volume accounts (acct-A, acct-B) experiencing request failures and retries. Support already notified. 
lee: Heap/kv cache size looked normal. The pattern suggests a kernel-level race when KV cache eviction and GPU buffer rebinds coincide under high concurrency. 
raj: For immediate mitigation: 1) Pause the v3.9.0 canary rollout 2) Rollback canary instances to v3.8.2 3) Scale down max-concurrency on remaining v3.9 nodes to 1 to quiesce. 
sophie: Doing 1 now. @deploy-bot, pause and rollback. 
deploy-bot: Canary pause accepted. Initiating rollback of 10% canary instances to v3.8.2. Estimated completion: 4m. ```kubectl rollout undo deployment/runtime --to-revision=202603150820 -n prod``` 
lee: I'm going to cordon gpu-cc-07 and gpu-cc-09 to stop scheduling and drain pods to avoid further OOMs. 
raj: Also adding a temporary node label to avoid autoscaler reusing same instance types. Command: ```kubectl label node gpu-cc-07 debug=isolated``` 
maria: Support update: sent initial message to acct-A and acct-B: "We're seeing elevated errors for inference requests in US-EAST. We're mitigating and will provide ETA in ~10 minutes." 
sophie: Rollback confirmed complete for canary. Metrics show error-rate dropping on mixed traffic but gpu-cc-07 still flapping. 
lee: On gpu-cc-07 kernel oops persists after container restart. Dumping dmesg: ```[ 1240.000123] kernel: show_stack+0x4f/0x80 
[ 1240.000130] kernel: RIP: 0010:0x7f9b3c1a2bcd 
[ 1240.000135] kernel: Code: ... 
[ 1240.000140] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000010 
[ 1240.000145] kernel: NIP: 0x7f9b3c1a2bcd``` 
raj: This aligns with a driver-level issue triggered by a recent NV driver microcode. I'm going to open a vendor support ticket. If we can repro with a small load, we can confirm. 
sophie: Repro plan: spin up a tiny canary in staging with v3.9.0 and run concurrent small-batch inference to try to hit the bad path. @raj can you lead? 
raj: On it. Spinning staging canary and running stress harness (concurrency=50, batch_size=8, model=vicuna-13b-q4). ```python stress.py --concurrency 50 --batch 8 --target staging-canary``` 
incident-bot: Handoff scheduled: sophie -> raj at 23:15 UTC. Next oncall ack required. 
sophie: Handing off to raj. I'm switching to support comms and customer outreach. 
raj: Update: reproduced in staging after ~90s. GPU process segfault + Xid 79. I've captured backtraces and will attach. Temporary mitigation successful: disabling continuous batching on v3.9.0 instances prevents immediate crash. Suggest we keep rollback + disable batching until vendor patch or deeper fix. 
lee: Agreed. Disabling continuous batching reduces perf but prevents kernel illegal access. Command applied via runtime config service. ```curl -X POST https://config.prod/internal/set -d '{"continuous_batching": false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'``` 
maria: Customer ETA update sent: "We've paused the canary and applied mitigations to prevent further restarts. We're seeing error rates return to baseline for most customers. We'll follow up with full RCA after vendor investigation." 
raj: Vendor ticket opened: NV-TSK-98765. Attaching dmesg, core dump, driver version: 545.45.17. Asked for priority escalation. 
sophie: Great. Action items: - Keep canary rolled back (sophie) - Keep continuous batching disabled on v3.9.0 until patch (raj) - Gather full core dumps and perf traces (lee) - Customer postmortem draft (maria) 
lee: I'll keep node cordoned until vendor confirms safe driver. Will also run memtest on gpu-cc-07 when maintenance window opens. 
raj: I'll run targeted fuzz tests on KV cache rebind paths. If we can create a small test case we can open PR to runtime to add defensive checks. 
sophie: If error rate remains low for next 30m, I'll mark incident as mitigated and move to monitoring. If anything spikes, re-open. 
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0453 status changed: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity remains P2. 
maria: Final note: no data exfiltration or request payload corruption reported. Only transient 502s and retries. Support will follow up with impacted customers to offer credits. 
raj: Adding timeline to ticket and linking this thread. Will update when vendor responds. 
sophie: Thanks team. Leaving the thread for follow-ups.
